title: Ambient integral direct image and the finite reduction tower
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite intermediate field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with $A=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi$, $I=(\varpi)$ and $P_n=A/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme morphism [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Put $A_Z=p_Z^*\underline A$ and $(P_n)_Z=p_Z^*\underline{P_n}$ for $Z=X,Y$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Then $A$ is Noetherian, each $P_n$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, and $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$ in degrees $-1,0$ is a finite free resolution of $P_n$. The canonical identifications
$$A_Z\cong\varprojlim_n(P_n)_Z,\qquad f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$$
identify these coefficients with the adic coefficient datum and its prescribed quotient maps [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum, sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x, sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients].

For every derived $\varpi$-complete $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$ [def-weil-derived-complete, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_X}(P_n)_X$ and let $M=Rf_{*,A}K$ be the ordinary, uncompleted ambient direct image [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Then $M$ is derived complete, the canonical coefficient-linear projection maps give isomorphisms
$$M\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,P_n}K_n,$$
and they commute with $P_{n+1}\to P_n$. They identify the completion map with an isomorphism
$$M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_n Rf_{*,P_n}K_n$$
in the derived strict-tower sense [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Here $\operatorname{Res}_n$ is restriction along $A_Y\to(P_n)_Y$. If a bounded-below étale $P_n$-complex $L_n$ and $K_n\cong\nu_X^*L_n$ are specified, then canonically
$$Rf_{*,P_n}K_n\cong\nu_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{ét},*,P_n}L_n,$$
where $\nu_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proét}}\to Z_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. No constructibility or properness is assumed for these comparisons.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(2),(3) and Lemma 5.4.3; agent specialization retaining the ordinary ambient coefficient action

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $A$ is a domain and every ideal is principal, so every ideal is finitely generated and $A$ is Noetherian. Its uniformizer is nonzero, hence multiplication by $\varpi^n$ is injective, with cokernel $P_n$ by the definition of that quotient. Thus $[A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A]$ in degrees $-1,0$, augmented to $P_n$, is the asserted finite free resolution. By [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], $P_n$ is finite. Since $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$, the element $\ell$ belongs to the maximal ideal $(\varpi)$, say $\ell=\varpi a$ with $a\in A$. Consequently $\ell^n=\varpi^n a^n$ annihilates $P_n$. In particular $A/I$ is additive torsion, and every $P_n$ is perfect. These verify every algebraic hypothesis in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(3), specialization to the DVR coefficient datum; elementary verification of its algebraic hypotheses

proof.text: The ring homeomorphism in [lem-sfb-integers-profinite-tower] identifies $A$ with $\varprojlim_nP_n$ through the reduction maps. By [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x], its pulled-back condensed ring $A_Z$ is canonically $\varprojlim_n(P_n)_Z$, and the finite coefficients here are the constant sheaves. The isomorphisms of [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] give $f^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ and $f^{-1}(P_n)_Y\cong(P_n)_X$. Their compatibility with the quotient projections is the explicit identity $\pi_{X,n}c_f=c_{f,n}f^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Thus both the coefficients and their specified quotient arrows are exactly the adic datum, rather than merely abstractly isomorphic ring sheaves.

source.place: Section 6.5 coefficient sheaves; Lemma 6.5.9, coefficient identification

proof.text: Use these ring identifications throughout. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], $M$ is computed by the total K-injective derived module direct image, with its induced $A_Y$-action. This is the ordinary ringed-topos direct image used below. The scalar-restriction comparisons of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] identify $Rf_{*,A}\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}$ with $\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}Rf_{*,P_n}$. In particular the finite-level target, after restriction, is $Rf_{*,A}(\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}K_n)$; its action has not been replaced by an arbitrary action on an isomorphic abelian complex. The cited comparison applies to strict coefficient systems as well as individual levels. Its auxiliary prime $p\ne\ell$ can be chosen arbitrarily: it imposes no characteristic condition on $X$ or $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition, applied to quotient restriction

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction], extending the free resolution of step 1 from the constant $A$-sheaf to $A_Z$ represents $(P_n)_Z$ by $[A_Z\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A_Z]$. In particular this is a perfect coefficient complex in the completed-coefficient ambient category. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula] to obtain, for every $n$, the canonical isomorphism
$$\pi_n:M\otimes^L_{A_Y}(P_n)_Y\longrightarrow Rf_{*,A}(\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}K_n)$$
in $D(A_Y)$, where the source is also viewed by restriction. There is no boundedness assumption on $K$ in this projection formula. This use is the perfect-coefficient case of Bhatt--Scholze Lemma 6.5.9(3); it does not infer a levelwise statement from the pro-object assertion 6.5.9(1).

Retain the quotient actions by constructing the morphism before restriction. On the strict system categories of [lem-pur-coefficient-system-derived-comparison], use the exact levelwise pullback $f_P^*$ and its derived right adjoint $Rf_{P,*}$. The hypothesis $A\cong\varprojlim P_n$ was checked in step 2. Form the strict derived reduction systems $B_Z$ of [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-pullback-derived-tower], retaining the $(P_n)_Z$-actions from their tensor construction. Exact inverse image commutes with derived coefficient change, so $f_P^*B_Y(M)\cong B_X(f_A^*M)$. Reduce the ambient counit $\varepsilon:f_A^*M\to K$ and take its adjunct. This gives
$$\beta:B_Y(M)\longrightarrow Rf_{P,*}B_X(K).$$
Its evaluations $\beta_n$ are morphisms in $D((P_n)_Y)$, and its construction is in the derived category of coefficient systems. By [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward], restriction of its target is $Rf_{*,A}^{\operatorname{Tow}}B_X(K)$. After restriction, its defining adjunct is exactly the tensor-pullback comparison followed by $\varepsilon\otimes1$. Therefore it is the morphism $h_K$ of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate], whose evaluations are $\pi_n$. By step 4 each restricted $\beta_n$ is an isomorphism. Exact restriction detects acyclic complexes, since it leaves the underlying abelian sheaves unchanged; applying this to the cone proves that each $\beta_n$ is an isomorphism in $D((P_n)_Y)$.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; counit-tensor mate on the coefficient diagram site

proof.text:
For $b\ge a$, the source transition of $\beta$ is induced by $q_{b,a}:P_b\to P_a$, and its target transition is derived direct image of the corresponding restricted transition of $K_\bullet$. On the tensor-pullback adjuncts the compatibility square reads
$$(1\otimes q_{b,a})\,(\varepsilon\otimes1)=(\varepsilon\otimes1)\,(1\otimes q_{b,a});$$
both composites send a local pure tensor $x\otimes u$ to $\varepsilon(x)\otimes q_{b,a}(u)$. The normalized strict-tower mate of [lem-weil-pbc-augmented-diagram-projection-mate] asserts this compatibility before evaluation and also gives
$$h_K i_{Y,M}=Rf_{*,A}^{\operatorname{Tow}}(i_{X,K})\chi_K.$$
Here $i$ is the quotient augmentation and $\chi$ the constant-tower comparison in that node. Thus the isomorphisms of step 5 commute with all quotient maps and, after restriction, constitute the specified augmented derived strict-tower comparison. They are not a choice of unrelated levelwise isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0A07, lemma-Rf-commutes-with-Rlim, strict tower interpretation; explicit quotient-transition square

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] to the derived complete $K$. It gives both completeness of the ordinary $M=Rf_{*,A}K$ and the canonical isomorphism
$$M\xrightarrow{\sim}R\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Res}_{Y,n}Rf_{*,P_n}K_n,$$
whose $n$-th projection is $Rf_{*,A}$ of $K\to\operatorname{Res}_{X,n}K_n$, followed by the coefficient-restriction comparison. For clarity, its limit comparison is the strict-tower comparison of [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison], obtained from $f_*\lim=\lim f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. The augmented equality in step 6 identifies this map with the completion map for $M$ after the reduction isomorphisms $\beta_n$: apply $R\lim$ to that equality and use the projection-normalized limit comparison. This proves the assertion for the canonical completion map, not just the existence of an isomorphism to the same limit object. All categories here are ordinary uncompleted ambient derived categories; completeness is a property of $M$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q63-707508a99 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 17 cited statements, unit sk-prop-open-coefficients, the parent step that cites the item (lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves step 2), and Bhatt–Scholze Lemma 5.4.3, Remark 5.4.4 and Lemma 6.5.9 with its proof (pp. 50–51). The delivery is one commit with no new nodes and the statement unchanged. The item was created 2026-10-21, so it is not in the dropped list, and the snapshot has no re-split note for it. All proof_deps exist and are unmerged. The transitive closure has 3233 nodes and contains neither the item nor its parent, so there is no cycle. The off-route citations (lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison, lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward, lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr) are generic tools declared in tool_uses; I accept them. The route follows the unit's integral paragraph: completeness (step 7), reduction through the two-term perfect resolution of P_n (steps 4–6, BS 6.5.9(3) rather than the pro-object clause (1)), and the étale comparison (step 8, BS 5.4.3/09A6, D^+ only). Step by step: step 1 (PID, so Noetherian; ϖ^n injective; ℓ=ϖa, so ℓ^n kills P_n; P_n perfect) matches every hypothesis of def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum. Step 2: the coefficient identifications and the projection identity π∘c_u=c_{u,n}∘u^{-1}π are stated by the cited nodes. Step 3: the auxiliary prime p in the cited completed-coefficient nodes plays no role in their statements. Step 4: the perfect projection formula holds for any morphism and unbounded K. Step 5: the map is built on (P_n)-systems through the coefficient-system adjunction and the diagram restriction/pushforward comparison, then identified with h_K by comparing adjuncts (a standard mate fact, compressed). Exact restriction then detects that each β_n is an isomorphism. Step 6: compatibility with transitions and the equation h_K i = G^Tow(i)χ_K are asserted before evaluation in the mate node. Step 7: since M is complete, the completion map is an isomorphism, and R lim of the levelwise isomorphism β is an isomorphism, so the stated clause follows; the extra normalization in the step is compressed but not needed. Step 8: Λ=P_n, f qcqs, L_n in D^+. Edge cases checked: n=1, E=Q_ℓ, ramified E, K=0, f=id, characteristic ℓ. No duplicate found: det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral, lem-sfb-admissible-direct-image and lem-sfb-adic-constructible-finite-reductions are narrower or different. No fixes. Advisory only: steps 5 and 7 compress the coherences noted above.
